Current animal models and pathogenic mechanisms of cholangitis and their translational relevance to CCA modeling

Current animal models and pathogenic mechanisms of cholangitis and their translational relevance to CCA modeling. (a): Schematic illustration of established animal models for cholangitis with their associated signaling pathways. The depicted models recapitulate key pathological features of human cholangitis through mechanisms involving TLR/NF-κB, ROS, and TGF-β/smad signaling. These inflammatory pathways drive persistent biliary injury and create a tumor-promoting microenvironment. (b): Summary of current experimental models for CCA development. The models are categorized by carcinogen-induced model, tumor implantation model, genetic engineering model, surgical animal model. The arrows indicate the likelihood of transformation between model methods. The sequential relationship between (a) and (b) indicates that there are many similarities between the modeling methods of inflammation model and cancer model, and the cholangitis model provides an important pathophysiological background for studying the inflammation-driven occurrence of CCA. CCA, Cholangiocarcinoma; ROS, reactive oxygen species
